text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on November 3 in history.
1492 - The Treaty of Etaples was signed between Charles VIII of France and Henry VII of England. Under the pact England renounced its claims to French territory in return for an indemnity.
1493 - Christopher Columbus discovered the island of Dominica. On this day in 1978 the country became independent.
1706 - An earthquake in the Italian town of Abruzzi killed 15,000 people.
1760 - Frederick the Great of Prussia defeated Austrian troops at Torgau in the Seven Years War.
1801 - Vincenzo Bellini born. Italian opera composer who earned international repute with works such as "Il Pirata" and "Norma".
1839 - The first Opium War between China and Britain began when British frigates blew up several Chinese junks off Canton after coming under attack.
1852 - Emperor Meiji of Japan born. Known as Prince Mutsuhito until he acceded to the throne in 1867, he was responsible for moving the capital from Kyoto to Edo which he renamed Tokyo.
1901 - King Leopold III of Belgium born. Became king in 1934 and led the army during the German conquest of the country in World War Two. Abdicated in favour of his son Baudouin in 1951.
1903 - Following a revolt, Panama declared itself independent of Colombia.
1912 - Alfredo Stroessner born. President of Paraguay from 1954 to 1989.
1918 - In World War One, part of the German fleet mutinied at Kiel, and the Allies signed an armistice with Austro-Hungary.
1921 - Charles Bronson, U.S. actor whose films include "The Magnificent Seven" and "Death Wish", born.
1926 - Annie Oakley, noted U.S. markswoman who starred in Buffalo Bill's Wild West Show, died.
1935 - A plebiscite in Greece returned George II to the throne. He had been in exile since 1923.
1954 - French artist Henri Matisse died. A fauvist, he is regarded as one of the most important French painters of the 20th century.
1957 - The Soviet Union launched the first inhabited space capsule, Sputnik II, carrying a dog called Laika.
1961 - The General Assembly unanimously elected U Thant Acting Secretary General of the U.N., following the death of Dag Hammarskjoeld.
1964 - Lyndon B. Johnson was elected U.S. president by a huge margin over Barry Goldwater.
1970 - Salvador Allende was sworn in as president of Chile, having won the election in October.

1975 - Queen Elizabeth opened an underwater pipeline to bring the first of Britain's North Sea oil ashore. 1978 - South African prime minister set up a judicial commission to investigate what became known as the "Muldergate Scandal". Cabinet minister Connie Mulder was accused of corruption.
1982 - Up to 1,000 Soviet soldiers and Afghan civilians died in an accident in the Salang tunnel in Afghanistan when a tanker exploded near Soviet military convoys.
1983 - In a referendum South Africans voted by a large majority to allow Indians and Coloureds some limited power-sharing in the government, but not blacks.
1986 - Joaquim Chissano was chosen to take over as President of Mozambique, following the death of Samora Machel in a plane crash in South Africa.
1988 - In South Korea an estimated 20,000 police stopped students from carrying out a threat to seize and kill former leader Chun Doo Hwan.
1989 - After weeks of demonstrations and the flight to the West of thousands, East German leader Egon Krenz pledged reforms and dismissed five members of his politburo.
1992 - Election day in the United States and voters elected Bill Clinton as President.
